subject: Anthropic's S-1: $16.3B revenue, $750B compute bill
bodyMarkdown:
If you own a Canadian index fund or a workplace pension, you already own a slice of the AI build-out second hand, through Nvidia and whatever cloud names your fund holds. Anthropic filed the paperwork for its share sale on Monday, and the real bill for that build-out is now written down in one public document.

## What is actually in the filing

Anthropic publicly filed its **S-1** on Monday, the registration statement a company lodges with American securities regulators before it can sell shares to the public. It plans to list Class A shares on the Nasdaq Global Select Market under the ticker ANT, with Goldman Sachs and Morgan Stanley leading the offering. The filing shows US$16.29 billion of revenue for the six months ended June 30, against a net loss of US$80.7 billion. Price and share count are left blank, which is normal this early. Reported targets put the valuation between US$1.5 trillion and US$2 trillion. In May the company raised US$65 billion privately at a post-money valuation of US$965 billion, so the ask is roughly double what investors paid five months ago. Markets took it well. Reuters reported Monday that Nvidia added nearly 3 per cent, with Micron up 3 per cent and AMD up 2.8 per cent.

## The loss everyone will quote

That US$80.7 billion will lead every story today, and it is the least informative line in the document. Reporting on the filing puts about US$72.4 billion of it down to changes in the fair value of convertible notes, derivative liabilities and SAFEs, which are instruments that turn into equity later and get revalued as the company's own price rises. No cash left the building. Take that out and the filing shows a first-half **GAAP operating loss** of US$693 million, meaning the loss from running the business under standard accounting rules, on US$16.29 billion of revenue. In the June quarter alone Anthropic posted a US$974 million operating profit, its first. The loss ballooned because the company became more valuable, which tells you about its capital structure and nothing about demand for Claude.

## The number I keep rereading

Compute. Fortune reported on Monday that the filing ties Anthropic to at least US$475 billion of future cloud purchases, climbing to as much as US$750 billion once chip leasing deals are counted, and that the company now intends to build data centres of its own. Other reads of the same filing land between US$542 billion and US$567 billion, so treat any single total loosely. The direction is not loose. Most of those commitments cannot be cancelled, and the filing admits the compute may not arrive, saying it may not get the full amount it seeks, or on the timelines it needs, even where contracts are in place. Customers, meanwhile, can walk away whenever they like, and Anthropic warns that pressure to cut token prices could shift its ratio of revenue to compute spending. Fixed bills for years against revenue that renews monthly.

## The takeaway

The number worth waiting for is the price range, which under SEC staff practice cannot be marketed before November 10, with the Wall Street Journal reporting a listing in the week of November 16. When it arrives, read the commitments note and the customer concentration section before you look at the revenue chart. The Fed and the Bank of Canada both decide tomorrow, and a raise reported at US$100 billion or more has to be funded into whatever rate market exists by then, so these two stories sit closer together than they look. I will not be buying at the open, and if you are tempted, wait for one quarter of numbers the company has to file with a regulator watching.
